newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach sees SWT meeting OPRAF criteria.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach sees SWT meeting OPRAF criteria.

text.p: British transport group Stagecoach Holdings Plc said on Friday that it was confident that its subsidiary South West Trains would meet the requirements set by OPRAF regarding train cancellations.

The Office of Passenger Rail Franchsing (OPRAF) said in a separate statement on Friday that it was planning to make an enforcement order against South West Trains (SWT), which, if imposed, would fine SWT one million stg.

The UK rail watchdog said the order would be imposed unless SWT ran at least 98.5 percent of scheduled services during April and they satisfied O'Brien that the recent level of cancellations would not happen again.
"Passengers on SWT have suffered an unacceptable level of cancellation in recent weeks," said John O'Brien, the franachising director of OPRAF.
If the fine is imposed then SWT would face losing its franchise if it failed to run at least 97.5 percent of its services.
Stagecoach was forced to cut services drastically after axing too many drivers in a cost cutting drive.
OPRAF and SWT have agreed a revised franchise plan which will see SWT commit one million stg of additional passenger service initiatives.
Stagecoach said it welcomed OPRAF's agreement to the revised franchise plans "which will bring additional benefits to SWT's passengers.
